corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 51, do not choose tensor or pipeline parallelism without measurements. Record the SLA with units (p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, TTFT and TPOT in ms), offered load, concurrency, throughput, prompt/output length mix, model and checkpoint, GPU count/type and memory headroom, interconnect topology, software and placement, batching policy, and availability target. State whether reconfiguration is allowed. Treat tokenizer, decoding, scheduler, power limits, request trace, load generator, warm-up, and compiler/cache state as controlled assumptions; do not present them as measured facts.

Pre-register a numerical falsifiable hypothesis: at a declared offered load and fixed quality, error, memory, and availability gates, one feasible strategy will reduce p99 end-to-end latency by at least a stated margin versus the alternative. Enumerate feasible tensor degrees and layer partitions, batch and microbatch settings. Randomize interleaved paired trials over identical requests, equalize warm-up and compilation, define sample size, exclusions, stopping rules, and uncertainty in advance, and keep tuning data disjoint from held-out evaluation. Measure per-GPU memory/utilization, tensor communication bytes and time, synchronization waits, layer imbalance, pipeline bubbles, queue depth, p50/p95/p99, TTFT/TPOT, requests/s, tokens/s, quality/error, cost, and failure/recovery time with units.

Control or stratify request lengths, topology, concurrency, thermal state, compiler/cache state, background load, and stragglers; label estimates and report confidence intervals. Reject a configuration if any quality, correctness, memory, error-rate, availability, or latency gate fails. Test failure and reconfiguration in a non-production environment, including worker/rank/link loss and restart, and restore the last known-good configuration if recovery time, error rate, memory, or tail latency breaches its gate.
